newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian steel mill in new investor rights row.
newsitem.headline: Russian steel mill in new investor rights row.

text.p: A shareholder in Russia's largest steel mill Novolipetsk Metals Combine said on Tuesday it had filed a new complaint against the plant, only weeks after a court ruled in its favour in a row over investor rights.

Russia-based Renaissance Capital's Sputnik investment fund said in a statement it had filed a complaint against mill management with the prosecutor in the Lipetsk region 400 km south of Moscow where the steel mill is based.
Sputnik said Novolipetsk had failed to include elections for a new board of directors in the published agenda of the annual shareholders meeting as Russian law required.
The statement said the mill had also set July 12 as the date for the meeting but that Russian law required the meeting to be held before June 30.
The prosecutor could take the dispute to court.

Last month a Lipetsk regional court ruled that the plant must include candidates from the Sputnik fund and fellow shareholders Russian Bank MFK and Cambridge Capital Management, on a list of nominees to the board of directors.
The ruling was hailed as a landmark victory for minority investors in Russia's often unruly emerging market.
The plaintiffs had claimed they were forcibly deterred from filing their candidates, while factory managers said they had acted according to company rules.
The Sputnik Fund owns nine percent of shares in the Novolipetsk combine. Cambridge Captital Management owns 17.2 percent and Bank MFK owns about 15 percent of plant shares.
